images.caption:
Lahinch seafront The Ordnance Survey of Ireland and Clare County Council appear unable to agree on the spelling of this small town on the coast of Liscannor Bay. Locals are convinced it should be 'Lahinch', but some signs and most maps state 'Lehinch'. 
This view of the multi-coloured houses on the seafront is taken from the road leading south towards Milltown Malbay.

images.caption:
Visited the Cathedral again and had to take some pictures.
Went with f/8 this time, 3 exposures at -2, 0 and +2 ev. Merged and processed in Photoshop CS6 Beta.

Aimed for the natural look so set most parameters to quite conservative values. Quite happy with the noise-free results.

images.filename: A WALK AROUND LIMERICK CITY IN JUNE - LITTLE PARK BEHIND THE HUNT MUSEUM (14402947752).jpg
images.caption:
Built in 1987 this footbridge is dedicated to the memory of Dr. Sylvester O'Halloran. The river crosses the Abbey River from the Potato Market to behind the Hunt Museum.

Sylvester O'Halloran (31 December 1728 – 11 August 1807) was an Irish surgeon with an abiding interest in Gaelic poetry and history. For most of his life he lived and practised in Limerick, and was later elected a member of the Royal Irish Academy (RIA).
